facts.fact: Article 324 vests superintendence, direction and control of elections to Parliament, legislatures, President and VP in the ECI.
Article 325 provides one general electoral roll per constituency with no exclusion on religion, race, caste or sex.
Article 326 provides adult suffrage at 18.
Articles 327 and 328 let Parliament and state legislatures make election laws.
Article 329 bars courts from electoral matters except through an election petition.
The ECI was set up on 25 January 1950, observed as National Voters' Day since 2011.
Sukumar Sen was the first Chief Election Commissioner.
Two ECs were added on 16 October 1989 and the posts abolished on 1 January 1990.
The ECI has been a multi-member body since October 1993.
T.N. Seshan v. Union (1995) upheld the multi-member ECI deciding by majority.
The Constitution does not fix the number of Election Commissioners; the ECI is not a five-member body (UPSC 2017).
Anoop Baranwal (2 March 2023) prescribed an interim panel of PM, Leader of Opposition and CJI.
Under the CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 the Selection Committee is the PM, the Leader of Opposition and a Union Cabinet Minister.
Under the 2023 Act a Search Committee headed by the Law Minister shortlists five names.
CEC/EC candidates must have held a post equal to Secretary to the Government of India.
The CEC and ECs serve six years or till 65, with salary equal to an SC judge.
The CEC is removed like an SC judge; an EC only on the CEC's recommendation.
The Constitution prescribes no qualifications for ECI members and does not bar retiring members from later posts.
The ECI itself notifies the election schedule, not the Home Ministry (UPSC 2017).
The ECI settles disputes on splits and mergers of recognised parties under the Symbols Order 1968 (UPSC 2017).
The ECI frames the Model Code of Conduct and allots party symbols.
The ECI advises the President or Governor on disqualification of legislators.
A state Chief Electoral Officer is appointed by the ECI in consultation with the state government; the Collector is District Election Officer.
Gyanesh Kumar is the 26th CEC, since 19 February 2025.
The Election Commissioners are Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi (October 2026).
The ECI does not conduct panchayat and municipal elections; State Election Commissions do.
Article 315 provides a PSC for the Union and each state and a Joint State PSC by Parliament on the states' request.
Article 316 covers appointment, term and an acting chairman.
Article 317 deals with removal and suspension of PSC members, only by the President.
Article 319 bars further government employment of PSC members after tenure.
Article 320 lists functions, 321 extension of functions, 322 charged expenses and 323 annual reports.
The first Public Service Commission was set up on 1 October 1926 on the Lee Commission's advice under Sir Ross Barker.
The Government of India Act 1935 created a Federal Public Service Commission, renamed UPSC in 1950.
About half of PSC members must have ten years of government service.
UPSC members serve six years or till 65; SPSC members six years or till 62.
PSC members may be removed for insolvency, paid outside employment or infirmity of mind or body.
Removal for misbehaviour needs an SC inquiry whose advice binds the President.
Being interested in a government contract counts as misbehaviour for a PSC member.
The UPSC chairman is barred from all government employment after tenure.
A UPSC member may later become chairman of the UPSC or of an SPSC only.
An SPSC chairman may later become UPSC chairman or member or chairman of another SPSC.
No PSC chairman or member gets a second term in the same office.
The UPSC recruits for the All India Services and central Group A and B services and advises on disciplinary matters.
PSC advice is not binding and failure to consult gives no remedy in court.
The UPSC is not consulted on reservations for backward classes or temporary appointments under a year.
Regulations excluding posts from the UPSC are laid before Parliament for 14 days.
Classification, pay, cadre and training lie with the DoPT, the central personnel agency.
The UPSC may serve a state on the Governor's request with the President's approval.
An SPSC reports to the Governor, and the report goes to the state legislature.
Ajay Kumar is the Chairman of the UPSC (October 2026).
A Joint State PSC is statutory; its members are appointed by the President and serve six years or till 62.
APPSC is an SPSC headquartered at Vijayawada.
Prof. C. Sashidhar has been in-charge Chairman of APPSC since A.R. Anuradha retired on 9 October 2025.
APPSC's Group-I 2026 notification has 166 vacancies, with applications till 27 October 2026.
Article 148: the CAG is appointed by the President by warrant and removed like an SC judge.
CAG duties under Article 149 are set by the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971.
Under Article 150 accounts are kept in the form the President prescribes on the CAG's advice.
Under Article 151 the CAG's reports go to the President or Governor, who lay them before the legislature.
The CAG serves six years or till 65 and is not eligible for further government office.
CAG office expenses are charged on the Consolidated Fund and no minister represents the CAG in Parliament.
The CAG audits the Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund and Public Account of the Union, states and UTs with a legislature.
The CAG certifies the net proceeds of taxes under Article 279 and the certificate is final.
The CAG submits three reports — Appropriation Accounts, Finance Accounts and Public Undertakings.
The CAG is the friend, philosopher and guide of the Public Accounts Committee.
Propriety audit is discretionary for the CAG; legal and regulatory audit is obligatory.
Secret service expenditure is a limitation on the CAG's audit.
Accounts were separated from audit at the Centre in 1976; the CAG still compiles state accounts.
India's CAG is only an Auditor-General with no control over the issue of money, unlike Britain's (UPSC 2012).
Ambedkar called the CAG the most important officer under the Constitution.
The CAG, SC, EC and UPSC are called bulwarks of democracy.
V. Narahari Rao was the first CAG.
K. Sanjay Murthy is the 15th CAG, since 21 November 2024.
The Finance Commission is constituted by the President every fifth year with a chairman and four members, eligible for reappointment.
The FC (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1951 wants a chairman experienced in public affairs and members including an HC-judge-qualified person and an economist.
The FC recommends division of net tax proceeds and principles of grants-in-aid.
Measures to augment state funds for panchayats and municipalities were added to FC functions by the 73rd and 74th Amendments.
Under Article 281 the FC report is laid before Parliament with an explanatory memorandum; advice is not binding.
K.C. Neogy chaired the first Finance Commission (1951).
The 15th FC under N.K. Singh fixed the states' share at 41%.
The 16th FC under Arvind Panagariya was constituted on 31 December 2023 for 2026-31.
The 16th FC report, tabled on 1 February 2026, kept the states' share at 41%.
Article 338 originally provided a Special Officer (Commissioner) for SCs and STs.
The 65th Amendment (1990) created a multi-member National Commission for SCs and STs.
The 89th Amendment (2003) split it into NCSC (Art 338) and NCST (Art 338A).
Each national commission has a chairperson, vice-chairperson and three members appointed by the President by warrant.
The commissions have the powers of a civil court.
Commission reports are laid before Parliament with an action-taken memorandum.
NCST duties include minor forest produce rights, PESA and ending shifting cultivation.
The Kaka Kalelkar (1953) and B.P. Mandal (1979) commissions were set up under Art 340.
After Indra Sawhney (1992) the NCBC was set up as a statutory body under the NCBC Act 1993.
The 102nd Amendment (2018) made the NCBC constitutional (Art 338B) and added Art 342A.
After the Maratha case (5 May 2021) the 105th Amendment restored the states' power to list SEBCs.
The Attorney General (Art 76) is appointed by the President and must be qualified to be an SC judge.
The AG's term is not fixed; he holds office during the pleasure of the President.
Under Art 88 the AG may speak in either House, a joint sitting and committees, but cannot vote.
The AG enjoys an MP's privileges (Art 105).
The AG is not a full-time counsel, may take private practice and is not a Cabinet member.
The Constitution does not require the AG to resign with the government; it is a convention (UPSC 2019).
The Solicitor General and Additional SGs are not constitutional posts and have no Art 88 right (UPSC 2019).
M.C. Setalvad was the first and longest-serving Attorney General.
The Advocate General (Art 165) is appointed by the Governor and must be qualified to be an HC judge.
The Advocate General may speak in the state legislature without a vote (Art 177) and has members' privileges (Art 194).
The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (Art 350B) was added by the 7th Amendment on the SRC's advice and is appointed by the President.
The Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities is headquartered at Prayagraj under the Ministry of Minority Affairs.
Article 350A asks states to provide mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage.
R. Venkataramani is the 16th Attorney General (since 1 October 2022), his term extended by two years in September 2025.
Tushar Mehta was re-appointed Solicitor General for three years in June 2026.
Kishor Makwana chairs the NCSC (October 2026).
Antar Singh Arya chairs the NCST (October 2026).
Sadhvi Niranjan Jyoti chairs the NCBC since March 2026.
Dammalapati Srinivas is the Advocate General of Andhra Pradesh since June 2024.
Anil Chandra Punetha is the State Election Commissioner of Andhra Pradesh.
The PAC has 22 members (15 Lok Sabha, 7 Rajya Sabha) and examines CAG reports (UPSC 2013).
By convention the PAC chair is from the Opposition.
The NDC has the PM, Union Cabinet Ministers and CMs; the Finance Commission Chairman is not a member (UPSC 2013).
The NDC, Planning Commission and Zonal Councils do not find mention in the Constitution (UPSC 2013).
An MLA's vote value in the presidential election varies by state; every MP's is equal (UPSC 2018).
A constitutional body is created by the Constitution; a statutory body by an Act; an executive body by a Cabinet resolution.
NITI Aayog (2015) is an executive body, not a constitutional one.
NHRC, CVC and Lokpal are statutory, not constitutional, bodies.
The Inter-State Council (Art 263) was set up in 1990.
SPSC members are appointed by the Governor but removed only by the President.
The GST Council (Art 279A) was created by the 101st Amendment and is chaired by the Union Finance Minister.
GST Council decisions need three-fourths of weighted votes, the Centre holding one-third and the states two-thirds.
Nirmala Sitharaman, the Union Finance Minister, chairs the GST Council.
The State Election Commission (Art 243K, 243ZA) runs panchayat and municipal elections, not Assembly polls.
The State Finance Commission (Art 243-I, 243-Y) is set up by the Governor every five years.
The AP Lokayukta is a statutory body under the AP Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act, 1983.
The AP SHRC is constituted under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 and is statutory.
The CAG is called the guardian of the public purse.
Sharing tax proceeds between the Centre and states is the Finance Commission's job, not the ECI's.
